items.caption: An oracle-script style redraw shows a compact enclosed loop above a larger branching figure. This reported early form is relevant to the conventional 女-plus-子 analysis, but its shapes alone do not establish the figures’ identities or 好’s original motivation.
items.alt: Black glyph with a small enclosed loop above a larger branching figure; a horizontal line joins them.
items.selection_reason: The redraw makes the reported size contrast visible, which is relevant to one interpretation of the 女 and 子 components. It does not resolve the proposed original meaning.
items.period: Shang oracle-script style; modern redraw, not a dated artifact specimen

items.caption: A bronze-script style redraw has a forked figure on the left and a rounded, open form on the right. Early forms are reported with 女 and 子 in variable positions; this redraw illustrates a contrasting arrangement, not a later stage in a sequence.
items.alt: Black glyph with a forked left figure and a rounded, open right-hand form.
items.selection_reason: Shows a contrasting component arrangement relevant to reported variation in placement, without suggesting chronological succession.
items.period: Bronze-script style; no specific specimen date established

limitations.text: 好’s original motivation remains unresolved. Proposed explanations include mother–child affection, a woman’s beauty, and affection between a man and a woman; cited early uses do not directly attest the mother–child interpretation.
These images are modern redrawings labeled by script tradition, not photographs of dated inscriptions. They illustrate reported forms but do not establish a verified chronological sequence.
